title: Pardons Edward J. DeBartolo Jr.
description_short: Trump pardoned former San Francisco 49ers owner Edward DeBartolo Jr., who had pleaded guilty in a corruption case.
description_medium: President Donald Trump pardoned former San Francisco 49ers owner Edward DeBartolo Jr., who had pleaded guilty to failing to report a felony after paying $400,000 to Louisiana Gov. Edwin Edwards in connection with a riverboat gambling license. The White House announced the pardon at an event with former NFL players.
description_long: President Donald Trump pardoned Edward J. DeBartolo Jr., the former owner of the San Francisco 49ers, in 2020. DeBartolo had pleaded guilty to failing to report a felony after paying $400,000 to Louisiana Gov. Edwin Edwards in connection with a riverboat gambling license. The pardon followed a federal corruption case tied to the state’s approval of riverboat gambling. DeBartolo had stepped down as the 49ers’ owner in 1997 after newspapers reported that he was expected to be indicted. The White House announced the pardon at an event attended by former NFL players, including Jerry Rice, Jim Brown, Ronnie Lott and Charles Haley. Haley called the episode a mistake that Trump had cleared. The pardon forgave DeBartolo’s federal offense; it was distinct from a commutation, which would only reduce a sentence. The announcement drew attention because Trump granted relief to a prominent sports figure whose team had won five Super Bowls under his ownership.
